text: You just died. Here's what happens to your body.
Your heart stops, so your blood stops carrying oxygen. Within minutes, your brain cells start to die.
But hearing may be one of the last things to go. Even when people can't respond, their brains can still react to sound.
Then every muscle in your body goes loose.
Your body starts cooling, about one and a half degrees every hour.
After about an hour, your blood sinks to the lowest parts of your body and leaves purple marks.
Then you get stiff. It starts in your jaw and eyelids, and by twelve hours, you're stiff all over.
About a day later, the stiffness fades, and your muscles go loose again.
And no, your hair and nails don't keep growing. Your skin dries and pulls back, so they just look longer.
And that's what happens to your body when you die.
